mainTopic: The מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע over תשרי or ניסן as the month of creation, the אבות and the גאולה, and the sources for events tied to פסח and ראש השנה
overview: This amud finishes רבי אליעזר's list of big events tied to תשרי. It then gives רבי יהושע's list, which moves creation, the birth and death of the אבות, and the future גאולה to ניסן. A ברייתא brings each side's proof that the world was created in their month, from the פסוקים of creation and from the season. Each side then explains away the other's פסוק. Next they argue over when the אבות were born, from 'ירח האיתנים' or 'חודש זיו'. This brings in רב יהודה's ברכה on blossoming trees. Both agree the אבות died in their birth month, because ה׳ completes the years of צדיקים exactly. The גמרא then proves that יצחק was born on פסח, working through pregnancy lengths and a leap year. It shows from two גזרות שוות that שרה, רחל and חנה were remembered on ראש השנה, and it begins the source that יוסף left prison on ראש השנה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי אליעזר's list: slavery ends, redemption past and future
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's list ends with three events: the slavery in מצרים stopped on ראש השנה, the redemption from מצרים came in ניסן, and the future redemption will come in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש השנה our forefathers stopped working as slaves in מצרים. In ניסן they were redeemed. In תשרי we will be redeemed in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of רבי אליעזר's list of major events that happened in certain months. These last items cover the end of the slavery, the redemption from מצרים, and the final גאולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that the world was created in תשרי, and he places the future גאולה in תשרי too. He still agrees that the actual Exodus happened in ניסן. The slavery itself stopped six months earlier, on ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: they are destined to be redeemed in the future (the final גאולה)

phrases.english: On Rosh HaShana the slave labor stopped
for our forefathers in Egypt;
in Nisan they were redeemed;
in Tishrei they will be redeemed in the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בָּטְלָה עֲבוֹדָה מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אליעזר's list of events from the ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slavery ended on ראש השנה, the Exodus was in ניסן, and the future גאולה will be in תשרי.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's list: most events placed in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע argues and places creation, the birth and death of the אבות, and the future גאולה in ניסן. He agrees about the events tied to ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: The world was created in ניסן. The אבות were born in ניסן and died in ניסן. יצחק was born on פסח. On ראש השנה, שרה, רחל and חנה were remembered by ה׳. On ראש השנה יוסף left prison. On ראש השנה the slavery in מצרים stopped. In ניסן we were redeemed, and in ניסן we will be redeemed in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives his own list, which disagrees with רבי אליעזר. For him the key month is ניסן, not תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three real disagreements: when the world was created, when the אבות were born and died, and when the future גאולה will be. On the items tied to ראש השנה, such as שרה, רחל and חנה being remembered, יוסף leaving prison, and the slavery ending, both תנאים say the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: was 'remembered' by ה׳, meaning she was blessed to have a child

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהושע disagrees about everything. The ראש השנה items match רבי אליעזר's list. The arguments are only about creation, the אבות, and the future גאולה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת about creation in תשרי or ניסן is the background for the rest of the סוגיא, which brings each side's proof.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
In Nisan the world was created;
in Nisan the Patriarchs were born;
in Nisan the Patriarchs died;
on Pesach Yitzchak was born;

phrases.aramaic: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נִפְקְדָה שָׂרָה רָחֵל וְחַנָּה,
phrases.english: on Rosh HaShana Sarah, Rachel, and Chana were remembered;
phrases.notes: 'Remembered' means ה׳ answered them and they became pregnant.

phrases.aramaic: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יָצָא יוֹסֵף מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: on Rosh HaShana Yosef came out of prison;
on Rosh HaShana the slave labor stopped
for our forefathers in Egypt;
in Nisan they were redeemed;
in Nisan they will be redeemed in the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: בְּנִיסָן נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Creation, the birth and death of the אבות, and the future גאולה are all in ניסן.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's proof that the world was created in תשרי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר's source. The פסוק 'תדשא הארץ' describes the earth sprouting grass while the trees are full of fruit, and that fits תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, how do we know the world was created in תשרי? The פסוק says, 'And ה׳ said: Let the earth sprout grass, plants giving seed, fruit trees.' Which month does the ground bring out new grass while the trees are full of fruit? It must be תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back and brings the source for each side, starting with רבי אליעזר. He reads the description of creation and matches it to the season of תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is to look at what nature looked like at creation and ask which month looks like that. In רבי אליעזר's reading, the grass was just starting to sprout while the trees already held fully grown fruit. That combination fits תשרי, the end of the summer harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
you must say; this is the only answer

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
From where do we know that the world was created in Tishrei?
As it is said:
"And God said: Let the earth sprout grass,
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:11

phrases.english: plants yielding seed, fruit trees."
Which is the month when the earth brings out grasses
and the tree is full of fruit?
You must say: this is Tishrei.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁבְּתִשְׁרִי נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two lists to the sources behind them, starting with רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaObject: That the world was created in תשרי
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 1:11, which describes sprouting grass and fruit trees, matched to the season of תשרי

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's second support: the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר adds that the time of creation was the season of the first rains, which made the plants grow. The פסוק 'ואד יעלה מן הארץ' shows this.
steps.simpleTranslation: That season was the time of the first rains. Rain fell and the plants sprouted, as the פסוק says: 'And a mist went up from the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר adds a second point to back up תשרי. Creation needed rain, and the rainy season starts around תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first proof came from the plants. This one comes from the rain that made them grow. The פסוק about the mist watering the ground shows that creation came with rain, and that fits the season that begins in תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: the time of the first rains that soak the ground
and a mist went up from the earth

phrases.english: And that period was the time of the first rains,
and rains fell and the plants sprouted,
as it is said: "And a mist went up from the earth."
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, rain-based support to רבי אליעזר's proof.
steps.raayaObject: That creation happened in the rainy season beginning in תשרי
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 2:6, the mist watering the ground

steps.title: רבי יהושע's proof that the world was created in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע reads the next פסוק, 'ותוצא הארץ', as describing ground full of grass while the trees are just starting to produce fruit, and that fits ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: how do we know the world was created in ניסן? The פסוק says, 'And the earth brought out grass, plants giving seed, and trees producing fruit.' Which month is the ground full of grass while the trees are starting to produce fruit? It must be ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי יהושע gives his source. He uses the same kind of reasoning but comes to ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע uses the very next פסוק, which tells what actually grew. In his reading the grass was already full and the trees were only beginning to give fruit. That is the picture of spring, which is ניסן.
steps.confusionAlert: The two proofs look almost the same, so watch the switch. רבי אליעזר has the ground bringing out new grass and trees full of fruit (תשרי). רבי יהושע has the ground already full of grass and trees just bringing out fruit (ניסן).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
From where do we know that the world was created in Nisan?
As it is said:
"And the earth brought out grass,
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:12

phrases.aramaic: עֵשֶׂב מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע וְעֵץ עוֹשֶׂה פְּרִי״.
phrases.english: plants yielding seed, and trees producing fruit."
Which is the month when the earth is full of grasses
and the tree brings out fruit?
You must say: this is Nisan.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁבְּנִיסָן נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing source, set up in parallel to רבי אליעזר's proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the world was created in ניסן
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 1:12, which describes the earth full of grass and trees beginning to bear fruit, matched to ניסן

steps.title: רבי יהושע's second support: the mating season of animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע adds that the time of creation was the season when animals and birds mate. The פסוק 'לבשו כרים הצאן' shows this season is spring.
steps.simpleTranslation: That season is the time when domestic animals, wild animals, and birds pair up with each other, as the פסוק says: 'The meadows are clothed with flocks...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע adds a second point to match רבי אליעזר's rain point. The newly created animals needed to have young to fill the world, and spring is their mating season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's extra support was about rain making plants grow. רבי יהושע's is about animals having young. The פסוק from תהלים pictures fields covered with flocks in spring, which shows that ניסן is when animals multiply.

keyTerms.meaning: domestic animals, wild animals, and birds
the meadows are clothed with flocks

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר says the world was created in תשרי: new grass, ripe fruit, and the rainy season. רבי יהושע says it was created in ניסן: full grass, budding trees, and the animals' mating season. Each one proves his month from the פסוקים of creation and from the season.

phrases.english: And that period
is the time when domestic animals, wild animals, and birds
mate with one another,
as it is said: "The meadows are clothed with flocks, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 65:14. 'וגו׳' just means the פסוק continues.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ הַפֶּרֶק, זְמַן בְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה וָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, animal-based support to רבי יהושע's proof, parallel to רבי אליעזר's rain support.
steps.raayaObject: That creation happened in the spring mating season, ניסן

steps.title: Challenge to רבי אליעזר from 'a tree making fruit'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבי אליעזר about 'עץ עושה פרי', which sounds like trees just starting to make fruit, as in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written, 'a tree making fruit'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבי יהושע's own פסוק against רבי אליעזר. 'Making fruit' sounds like the fruit is only beginning, which fits spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said the world was created in תשרי, when trees are already full of fruit. But the פסוק of 'ותוצא הארץ' says 'עץ עושה פרי', a tree in the middle of producing fruit. That fits ניסן better, so רבי אליעזר has to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)
A tree making fruit, still in the process

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here is רבי אליעזר, who holds the world was created in תשרי.

phrases.english: isn't it written: "a tree making fruit"!
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the wording of רבי יהושע's פסוק from step 5 against רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that creation was in תשרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Making fruit' means the fruit is just starting, which is a ניסן picture and not a תשרי one.

steps.title: 'Making fruit' is a blessing for the future
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that 'עץ עושה פרי' is a blessing for future generations, not a picture of the moment of creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is written as a blessing for future generations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers that 'making fruit' is not describing that first day. It is a blessing that trees will keep making fruit in every generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words describe what trees will do from then on, not what they looked like when created. So the trees could still have been full of fruit at creation in תשרי, and the challenge falls away.

phrases.english: That one is a blessing for the generations
that is what it is written for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Making fruit' describes the trees at the moment of creation, so it must have been spring.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Making fruit' is a blessing for all future generations, so it says nothing about the season of creation.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי יהושע from 'a fruit tree'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבי יהושע about 'עץ פרי', which sounds like trees already full of fruit, as in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written, 'a fruit tree'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא does the same thing in the other direction. It uses רבי אליעזר's פסוק, which calls it a 'fruit tree', against רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said creation was in ניסן, when fruit is just starting. But 'עץ פרי', a fruit tree, sounds like a tree already loaded with fruit. That fits תשרי better.

keyTerms.meaning: A fruit tree, already full of fruit

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: This time 'the other one' is רבי יהושע, who holds the world was created in ניסן.

phrases.english: isn't it written: "a fruit tree"?
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:11

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 7 by using רבי אליעזר's פסוק from step 3 against רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's view that creation was in ניסן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Fruit tree' implies the fruit is already there, which is a תשרי picture.

steps.title: Creation came out fully grown
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers with רבי יהושע בן לוי: everything in creation was made in its full, finished form, so trees had fruit even in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That fits רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: everything in creation was made at full height, with full understanding, and in full form. As it says, 'And the heavens and the earth and all their host were finished.' Don't read it as 'their host' (צבאם). Read it as 'their form' (צביונם).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers that the trees really did have fruit at creation. That isn't because of the season, but because everything was created already complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that everything was created at full size, with full understanding, and in its full form. So a tree full of fruit at creation does not show it was autumn. It was made fully grown even in ניסן. He learns this by reading 'צבאם' as 'צביונם'.

keyTerms.meaning: In their full form or appearance
Don't read it as… (reading a word a new way)

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that creation came out complete and fully grown, is a well-known teaching that shows up in other places too.

phrases.english: That one is like רבי יהושע בן לוי.
For רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
All the works of creation were created at their full height,
they were created with their full understanding,
they were created in their full form,
as it says: "And the heavens and the earth and all their host were finished,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:1

phrases.english: do not read "their host,"
but rather "their form."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing in an outside principle (רבי יהושע בן לוי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A tree full of fruit at creation proves it was the autumn season.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything was created fully finished, so ripe fruit says nothing about the season.

steps.title: The אבות were born in תשרי, the 'month of the mighty'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא returns to רבי אליעזר, who proves the אבות were born in תשרי from the name 'ירח האיתנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: How do we know the אבות were born in תשרי? Because it says, 'All the men of Israel gathered to King שלמה in the month of the איתנים, at the חג.' That is the month in which the mighty ones of the world were born.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from creation to the next claim, the birth of the אבות. רבי אליעזר brings a פסוק calling תשרי 'the month of the איתנים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the gathering on the חג (סוכות) refers to תשרי. רבי אליעזר reads 'איתנים' as the mighty ones, meaning the אבות, so it is the month they were born.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of the mighty ones (תשרי)
The mighty ones of the world, meaning the אבות

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:
From where do we know that the forefathers were born in תשרי?
As it says: "And they gathered to King שלמה,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:2

phrases.english: all the men of Israel,
in the month of the איתנים, at the festival,"
phrases.notes: The festival is סוכות, which is in תשרי.

phrases.english: the month in which the mighty ones of the world were born.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁבְּתִשְׁרִי נוֹלְדוּ אָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the back-and-forth about creation and returns to the ברייתא's next claim, the birth of the אבות.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's claim that the אבות were born in תשרי

steps.title: How do we know 'איתן' means mighty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the word 'איתן' means strong or mighty.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word 'איתן' means mighty ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The proof in step 11 depends on 'איתנים' meaning 'mighty ones'. The גמרא stops to ask where that meaning comes from, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'איתנים' just meant something else, the link to the אבות would not work. So the גמרא wants proof of the word's meaning before accepting the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: How is it implied? How do we know?
A word that means strong ones

phrases.english: From where is it implied
that this word "איתן" is a term for strong ones?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the key word in the proof of step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that 'איתן' means mighty or strong

steps.title: פסוקים showing 'איתן' means mighty, and the merit of the אבות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings three פסוקים: 'איתן מושבך', 'והאיתנים מוסדי ארץ', and the leaping over mountains, which is read as the merit of the אבות and אמהות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'Strong (איתן) is your dwelling.' And it says, 'Hear, mountains, the argument of ה', and you strong ones (איתנים), foundations of the earth.' And it says, 'The voice of my beloved, here he comes, leaping over the mountains, skipping over the hills.' 'Leaping over the mountains' means in the merit of the אבות. 'Skipping over the hills' means in the merit of the אמהות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with פסוקים where 'איתן' clearly means strong. It also shows that 'mountains' and 'איתנים' refer to the אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows that 'איתן' means strong. The second puts 'איתנים' next to 'mountains'. The third shows that mountains stand for the אבות, since redemption comes 'leaping over the mountains', in their merit. So 'איתנים' are the mighty אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: And it also says (bringing another פסוק)
The foremothers: שרה, רבקה, רחל, לאה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר learns that the אבות were born in תשרי from 'ירח האיתנים'. 'איתנים' means the mighty ones, and the אבות are called mountains and mighty ones.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Strong is your dwelling,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:21

phrases.english: and it says: "Hear, mountains, the argument of ה',
phrases.notes: מיכה 6:2

phrases.english: and you strong ones, foundations of the earth,"
and it says: "The voice of my beloved, here he comes,
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 2:8

phrases.aramaic: מְדַלֵּג עַל הֶהָרִים מְקַפֵּץ עַל הַגְּבָעוֹת״.
phrases.english: leaping over the mountains, skipping over the hills."
"Leaping over the mountains" means in the merit of the forefathers.
"Skipping over the hills" means in the merit of the foremothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'איתן' means strong (במדבר 24:21). 'איתנים' appears next to 'mountains' (מיכה 6:2), and mountains stand for the אבות (שיר השירים 2:8).

steps.title: רבי יהושע proves the אבות were born in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע brings a פסוק calling the month of building the בית המקדש 'חודש זיו', the month of the shining ones of the world, meaning the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: How do we know the אבות were born in ניסן? The פסוק says the בית המקדש was built in 'the month of זיו', the month when the shining people of the world were born.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the ברייתא gives רבי יהושע's side. He proves the אבות were born in ניסן from the name 'חודש זיו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as רבי אליעזר read 'איתנים' as the strong ones (the אבות), רבי יהושע reads 'זיו' (shine) as 'זיוותני עולם', the shining ones of the world. For him, חודש זיו is the month in which the אבות were born, and he holds that is ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of זיו (shine), from the פסוק about building the בית המקדש
The shining ones of the world, meaning the אבות

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
From where do we know that the Patriarchs were born in Nisan?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי בִשְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה וְאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה
phrases.english: As it says: "And it was in the four hundred and eightieth year
phrases.notes: מלכים א 6:1, about when שלמה began building the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: after the Children of Israel left the land of Egypt,
in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv"
meaning the month in which the radiant ones of the world were born.
phrases.notes: He hears 'זיו' (shine) as a hint to the shining people of the world, the אבות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁבְּנִיסָן נוֹלְדוּ אָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing proof to רבי אליעזר's 'ירח האיתנים' from Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That the אבות were born in ניסן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 6:1, 'בחודש זיו', read as the month of the 'זיוותני עולם'.

steps.title: How does רבי יהושע explain 'ירח האיתנים'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבי יהושע: there is a פסוק calling תשרי 'the month of the mighty ones', which sounds like the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too, רבי יהושע: isn't it written 'in the month of the mighty ones'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע with רבי אליעזר's פסוק. If תשרי is called the month of the mighty ones, doesn't that mean the אבות were born then?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has a פסוק, so each side has to explain the other's פסוק. Here the pressure is on רבי יהושע: what does 'איתנים' mean to him if not the אבות?

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one too: how does he deal with this?
The month of the mighty ones, meaning תשרי

phrases.english: And the other one as well,
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here is רבי יהושע, who said ניסן.

phrases.english: isn't it written: "In the month of the mighty ones"!
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:2.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי אליעזר's proof into a challenge against רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's view that the אבות were born in ניסן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls תשרי the month of the 'איתנים', which was shown to mean the strong ones, the אבות.

steps.title: תשרי is strong in מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע reads 'איתנים' as the month being strong with many מצוות, not as a hint to the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it means the month is strong in מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers that 'איתנים' describes the month itself, which is packed with מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees 'איתן' means strong. He just says the strength belongs to the month, with all its ימים טובים and their מצוות, and not to people born in it.

phrases.english: There, it means that it is mighty in מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word: the strength belongs to the month, not to the אבות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'איתנים' means the strong people, the אבות, born in תשרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'איתנים' means תשרי is strong in מצוות, so it says nothing about the אבות' birth.

steps.title: How does רבי אליעזר explain 'חודש זיו'?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns to רבי אליעזר: how does he explain 'חודש זיו'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too, רבי אליעזר: isn't it written 'in the month of זיו'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the same move in the other direction. It challenges רבי אליעזר with רבי יהושע's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'זיו' hints to the shining ones of the world, רבי אליעזר seems contradicted. He needs a different meaning for 'זיו'.

phrases.english: And the other one as well,
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' is רבי אליעזר, who said תשרי.

phrases.english: isn't it written: "In the month of Ziv"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of Step 15, now aimed at רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that the אבות were born in תשרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names the month after 'זיו', which רבי יהושע read as the shining people born then.

steps.title: זיו means the shine of the trees
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads 'זיו' as the beauty of the trees blossoming in that season.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק means it is a month that has shine for the trees.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers that 'זיו' describes nature in spring, not the אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יהושע did with 'איתנים', רבי אליעזר keeps the plain meaning of the word but changes what it describes. The shine belongs to the blossoming trees, not to people born then.

phrases.english: That one means it is the month in which there is radiance for the trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word: the shine belongs to the trees, not to the אבות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זיו' hints to the shining ones, the אבות, born in that season.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זיו' refers to the spring beauty of trees in bloom.

steps.title: רב יהודה's ברכה on blossoming trees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the 'trees' reading with רב יהודה's ruling that one says a special ברכה on seeing trees blossom in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said: someone who goes out in the days of ניסן and sees trees blossoming says: Blessed is He Who left nothing lacking in His world, and created in it good creatures and good trees for people to enjoy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last answer. It shows that ניסן really is known as the special time when trees blossom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since חז"ל set a ברכה for this sight in ניסן, it makes sense that the פסוק would name the season after the trees' shine. This is the source of the well-known ברכת האילנות.

keyTerms.meaning: To enjoy, to have pleasure from

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for ברכת האילנות, which people say in ניסן to this day.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said:
One who goes out during the days of Nisan
and sees trees that are blossoming recites:
Blessed is He Who has withheld nothing from His world,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָרָא בּוֹ בְּרִיּוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְאִילָנוֹת טוֹבוֹת
phrases.english: and has created in it beautiful creatures and beautiful trees
for human beings to enjoy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That ניסן is the time known for the shine of the trees.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's ברכה on seeing blossoming trees in ניסן.

steps.title: The אבות died in the same month they were born
steps.stepSummary: Whoever says the אבות were born in ניסן says they died in ניסן; whoever says תשרי says they died in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says they were born in ניסן says they died in ניסן. The one who says they were born in תשרי says they died in תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new point both sides agree on. The אבות died in the same month they were born, whichever month that was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides still argue about which month. But both agree on the idea that the אבות' lives ended in the very month they began. The next step brings the source.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says, meaning whichever opinion holds

phrases.english: The one who said they were born in Nisan
holds that in Nisan they died.
The one who said they were born in Tishrei
holds that in Tishrei they died,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּנִיסָן נוֹלְדוּ בְּנִיסָן מֵתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how each side reads the פסוקים, the ברייתא adds a shared idea about when the אבות died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to both views, the אבות died in the same month they were born.

steps.title: משה said 'today' I am 120
steps.stepSummary: The proof is from משה's words 'I am 120 years old today'. The extra word 'היום' teaches that his years were completed to the exact day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He said to them, I am 120 years old today.' There was no need to say 'today'. So why does it say 'today'? To teach: today my days and years are filled.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to prove that a צדיק can die on the very date he was born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows משה spoke on that day, so the word 'היום' seems extra. The extra word teaches that his age was exactly 120 on that day: he died on his birthday.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק needs to say. 'אין תלמוד לומר' means there was no need to say it.

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is about משה, not the אבות. It teaches a general rule about צדיקים, which the ברייתא then applies to the אבות.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם״,
phrases.english: I am one hundred and twenty years old today"
phrases.notes: דברים 31:2. משה says this on the day he died.

phrases.english: For there is no need for the verse to say "today",
so why does the verse say "today"?
It means: today my days and years are filled.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם בֶּן מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That צדיקים die on the exact date they were born.

steps.title: הקדוש ברוך הוא completes the years of צדיקים exactly
steps.stepSummary: The lesson: ה׳ fills the years of צדיקים exactly, day for day and month for month, as the פסוק says 'I will fill the number of your days'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches you that הקדוש ברוך הוא sits and fills the years of צדיקים from day to day and from month to month, as it says: 'The number of your days I will fill.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states the general lesson from משה's 'today' and backs it with another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From day to day' means a צדיק's life ends on the same date it began, with no partial year. That is why the אבות died in their birth month. The פסוק in שמות promises exactly this full count of days.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר says the אבות were born in תשרי ('איתנים'), and רבי יהושע says ניסן ('זיו'). Each one rereads the other's word: strong in מצוות, or the shine of trees. Both agree the אבות died in their birth month, because ה׳ completes the years of צדיקים exactly.

phrases.english: This teaches you that the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits
and fills the years of the righteous
from day to day and from month to month,
phrases.notes: The life of a צדיק ends on the same date it started.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "The number of your days I will fill."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:26.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב וּמְמַלֵּא שְׁנוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the general lesson drawn from the 'היום' in Step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ה׳ completes the years of צדיקים to the exact day, so the אבות died in the same month they were born.

steps.title: Source for יצחק being born on פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the ברייתא's claim that יצחק was born on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: יצחק was born on פסח. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, that יצחק was born on פסח, and asks for its source. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with whether the אבות were born and died in ניסן or in תשרי. Now the ברייתא makes a specific claim about יצחק, and the גמרא wants a פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival of Passover, in ניסן
Isaac, son of אברהם and שרה
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: On Passover Isaac was born. From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general ניסן/תשרי debate to a specific claim about יצחק's birth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that יצחק was born on פסח.

steps.title: The angel's promise: 'At the appointed time I will return'
steps.stepSummary: The source is the angel's words to אברהם: 'למועד אשוב אליך'. The word מועד is read as a festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'At the appointed time I will return to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the angel's promise to אברהם that he will come back 'at the מועד'. מועד here is read as a festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the birth will happen at a festival but does not say which one. The next steps work out which festival it must be.

keyTerms.meaning: An appointed time; here read as a festival
At the appointed time I will return to you

phrases.english: As it is written: 'At the appointed time I will return to you.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:14. The angel is telling אברהם that שרה will have a son by then.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The angel promised the birth for the next festival (מועד).

steps.title: Could the angel have spoken on פסח?
steps.stepSummary: If the angel spoke on פסח and meant the next festival, עצרת, that leaves only fifty days, which is impossible for a pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: When was the angel speaking? If you say it was on פסח and he meant עצרת, can a woman give birth after fifty days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks on which festival the angel spoke. It tests the first option, פסח, and rejects it because the next festival, עצרת, is only fifty days later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'I will return at the מועד' means the next festival after the one when the angel spoke. Going from פסח to עצרת gives only fifty days, far too short for a pregnancy.

keyTerms.meaning: When was he standing, meaning on what date was this said?

phrases.english: When was he standing?
phrases.notes: He means: on what day did the angel say this to אברהם?

phrases.english: If you say it was on Passover
and he told him she would give birth on Shavuot
can she give birth in fifty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts testing which festival the פסוק means.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the angel spoke on פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fifty days is too short for a pregnancy.

steps.title: Could the angel have spoken on שבועות?
steps.stepSummary: If the angel spoke on עצרת and meant the festival in תשרי, that is still only five months, which is also too short.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say he was standing on עצרת and told him the birth would be in תשרי. Still, can she give birth after five months?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option: the angel spoke on עצרת about the next festival, in תשרי. It rejects this too, because five months is still too short.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each option moves the starting point one festival later. From עצרת to the festival in תשרי is about five months, and a baby is not born that early.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of the fall festivals

phrases.english: Rather, he was standing on Shavuot
and he told him it would be in Tishrei

phrases.aramaic: אַכַּתִּי בְּחַמְשָׁה יַרְחֵי מִי קָא יָלְדָה?
phrases.english: Still, can she give birth in five months?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected option of step 25 with the next festival, then rejects it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the angel spoke on עצרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Five months is still too short for a pregnancy.

steps.title: The angel spoke on סוכות about ניסן
steps.stepSummary: The remaining option is that the angel spoke on סוכות (חג) and promised a birth on פסח in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was standing on סוכות and told her it would be in ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on the last option: the angel spoke on סוכות, and the next festival is פסח. This is how we know יצחק was born on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only this option gives enough time for a pregnancy. So the 'מועד' in the פסוק is פסח, which supports the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, he was standing on the Festival (Sukkot)
and he told her it would be in Nisan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקָאֵי בְּחַג וְקָאָמַר לַהּ בְּנִיסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Arrives at the only workable option after rejecting the first two.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The angel spoke on פסח or עצרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The angel spoke on סוכות and promised a birth on פסח.

steps.title: Six months is still too short
steps.stepSummary: Even from סוכות to פסח is only six months. Can a woman give birth that soon?
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, can she give birth after six months?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. From סוכות to פסח is only six months, which also seems too short for a pregnancy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elimination left סוכות to פסח, but six months still looks like an impossible pregnancy length. The proof is now in question.

phrases.english: Still, in six months
can she give birth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַכַּתִּי, בְּשִׁיתָּא יַרְחֵי מִי קָא יָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 27.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Six months is too short for a viable birth.

steps.title: That year was a leap year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the year was a leap year. An extra month was added, so the time was about seven months.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: that year was a leap year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא saying that year had an extra month. That makes the gap from סוכות to פסח about seven months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leap year adds a second אדר before ניסן. Seven months is a known length for a pregnancy, so the timeline now works.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A leap year, which has an extra month

phrases.english: It was taught: that year was a leap year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a fact about the calendar
steps.terutzMaskana: With the extra month, about seven months passed.

steps.title: Subtracting the days of impurity leaves less than seven months
steps.stepSummary: Even in a leap year, if you take away שרה's days of טומאה, there are not quite seven full months.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, when the master subtracts the days of impurity, they come up short.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. Once you take away the days of טומאה, the seven months are no longer complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרה could not have conceived during her days of טומאה, so they cannot count toward the pregnancy. That leaves a bit less than seven full months, and the timeline looks too short again.

keyTerms.meaning: They are lacking, they fall short

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף סוֹף, כִּי מַדְלֵי מָר יוֹמֵי טוּמְאָה —
phrases.english: In the end, when the master subtracts the days of impurity
phrases.notes: He means the days she was טמאה before she could conceive. Those days come off the total.

phrases.english: they come up short!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, כִּי מַדְלֵי מָר יוֹמֵי טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the leap-year answer of step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The seven-month timeline from the leap year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking away the days of טומאה leaves less than seven full months.

steps.title: A seven-month baby can be born early
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא: a seven-month baby does not need complete months. From the פסוק about חנה, the minimum is six months and two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Even according to the one who says a woman giving birth in the ninth month does not give birth to incomplete months, a woman giving birth in the seventh month does give birth to incomplete months. As it says: 'And it came to pass at the cycles of the days.' The minimum of 'cycles' is two, and the minimum of 'days' is two.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers that a seventh-month birth can come before the seventh month is complete. This fixes the problem of the missing impurity days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about חנה's birth of שמואל uses plurals: 'cycles' (seasons of three months) and 'days'. The smallest plural is two, so two seasons (six months) plus two days is enough. Even after taking away the days of טומאה, שרה's pregnancy was longer than that.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives birth before the months are complete
The minimum, the smallest amount a plural word can mean

steps.whatToRemember: יצחק was born on פסח: the angel spoke on סוכות, it was a leap year, and a seventh-month baby can be born after six months and two days.
steps.confusionAlert: מר זוטרא is not saying any baby can come at six months. He is saying a baby born in the seventh month can arrive before that month is complete, at the earliest after six months and two days.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
Even according to the one who says that one who gives birth at nine months
does not give birth before the months are complete,
one who gives birth at seven months can give birth before they are complete,
as it says: 'And it came to pass at the cycles of the days,'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:20, about חנה giving birth to שמואל.

phrases.english: the minimum of 'cycles' is two,
and the minimum of 'days' is two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the impurity-days challenge of step 30 and closes the יצחק discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A rule about pregnancy length, learned from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A seven-month birth needs seven full months.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seventh-month birth can come after six months and two days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This short rule about the minimum length of a seventh-month pregnancy is what lets the whole פסח timeline for יצחק stand.

steps.title: שרה, רחל and חנה were remembered on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says שרה, רחל and חנה were remembered by ה׳ (and conceived) on ראש השנה. The גמרא asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש השנה שרה, רחל and חנה were remembered. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the ברייתא and asks how we know it. This sets up רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new claim about the date the three women were remembered and conceived. The גמרא now needs a source tying their stories to ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year, on א׳ תשרי
Was remembered by ה׳, here meaning she conceived

phrases.english: On Rosh Hashanah were remembered
Sarah, Rachel and Hannah. From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נִפְקְדָה שָׂרָה רָחֵל וְחַנָּה. מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יצחק timeline and opens a new line of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that these women were remembered on ראש השנה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's verbal link through 'remembering'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר uses a גזרה שוה. 'Remembering' is used for רחל and חנה, and also for ראש השנה ('זכרון תרועה'), so they were remembered on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It comes from 'remembering' and 'remembering,' and from 'visiting' and 'visiting.' It is written about רחל: 'And ה׳ remembered רחל,' and about חנה: 'And ה׳ remembered her.' And 'remembering' is learned from 'remembering' with ראש השנה, as it is written: 'A day of rest, a remembrance of the שופר blast.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers with a גזרה שוה: the same word in two places links them. Because רחל and חנה were 'remembered', and ראש השנה is called a day of 'remembrance', they were remembered on ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two links. The word זכירה connects רחל and חנה to ראש השנה. The word פקידה is the second link, which ties שרה to them. This step spells out the זכירה link; the next step spells out the פקידה link.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from; used for a גזרה שוה
A remembrance of the שופר blast, a name for ראש השנה

steps.whatToRemember: רחל and חנה were 'remembered' on ראש השנה, learned by a גזרה שוה from 'זכרון תרועה'. The word 'פקידה' will be the link for שרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
It is learned from 'visiting' and 'visiting,'
phrases.notes: This link is for שרה. The next step spells it out.

phrases.english: and it is learned from 'remembering' and 'remembering.'
It is written about Rachel: 'And God remembered Rachel,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 30:22.

phrases.english: and it is written about Hannah: 'And ה׳ remembered her,'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:19.

phrases.english: and 'remembering' is learned from 'remembering' with Rosh Hashanah,
as it is written: 'A day of rest, a remembrance of the shofar blast.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה on זכירה links רחל and חנה to ראש השנה, and a second link on פקידה will bring in שרה.

steps.title: Linking שרה to חנה through the word 'visited' (פקידה)
steps.stepSummary: A second גזרה שוה uses the word פקידה, found by both חנה and שרה, to show that שרה was also remembered on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Visiting' and 'visiting': about חנה it says 'For ה׳ visited חנה', and about שרה it says 'And ה׳ visited שרה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אלעזר's answer from the last step. It now brings שרה into the proof too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 33, the word 'זכירה' linked רחל and חנה to ראש השנה. But the פסוק about שרה does not use 'זכירה'. It uses 'פקידה'. So a second link is needed: חנה has both words, and שרה shares 'פקידה' with her. That means שרה was also remembered on ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: ה׳ 'remembering' or 'visiting' someone, here meaning He blessed her with a child
Learning one place from another because the same word is used in both

steps.confusionAlert: This is a chain of two links. שרה connects to חנה through 'פקידה'. Then חנה connects to ראש השנה through 'זכירה'. שרה is never linked to ראש השנה directly.

phrases.english: "Visiting" and "visiting":
phrases.notes: The same word shows up in two places, so the גמרא links them. This is a second גזרה שוה.

phrases.english: It is written about חנה:
"For ה׳ visited Chana,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:21

phrases.english: and it is written about שרה:
"And ה׳ visited Sarah."
phrases.notes: בראשית 21:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי אלעזר's derivation by adding שרה through a second word link
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שרה is linked to חנה by the word 'פקידה'. Since חנה was remembered on ראש השנה, so was שרה.
steps.whatToRemember: All three women were remembered on ראש השנה. רחל and חנה are linked through 'זכירה', and שרה is linked through 'פקידה' to חנה.

steps.title: Asking for the source that יוסף left prison on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, that יוסף left prison on ראש השנה, and asks how we know this.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש השנה יוסף came out of prison. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next claim in the same ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed several events that happened on ראש השנה. The women's case is done, so now the גמרא checks the claim about יוסף. It asks which פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: יוסף, the son of יעקב, who was in prison in Egypt
Prison, literally 'the house of the bound ones'
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: On ראש השנה יוסף came out
phrases.notes: This is the next line of the same ברייתא from step 32.

phrases.english: of prison.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יָצָא יוֹסֵף מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the women to the next claim in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that יוסף left prison on ראש השנה

steps.title: A פסוק about blowing שופר on the festival at the new month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with a פסוק from תהלים about blowing שופר at the new month. That points to ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Blow the שופר at the new month, at the covered time, for our festival day. For it is a law for Israel, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering by quoting a פסוק that talks about ראש השנה. The part that connects it to יוסף comes in the next words of the passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing שופר 'at the new month' on a 'festival day' fits only ראש השנה. It is the one festival that falls when the moon is hidden at the start of the month. The 'וגו׳' tells us the passage keeps going. Those next words tie this day to יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: At the covered time, when the moon is hidden

steps.confusionAlert: The words quoted here do not mention יוסף yet. They only show that the passage is about ראש השנה. The link to יוסף comes from the words that follow.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Blow the שופר at the new month,
phrases.notes: תהלים 81:4–5

phrases.english: at the covered time, for our festival day.
phrases.notes: 'Covered' means the moon is hidden. Only ראש השנה is a festival at that point in the month.

phrases.english: For it is a law for Israel, etc."
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the פסוק keeps going. The next words are what connect this day to יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about יוסף
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק in תהלים describes ראש השנה. The passage continues with words that are connected to יוסף.
